newsitem.title: UK: Cash Brent mixed as July slips, spreads edge highe.
newsitem.headline: Cash Brent mixed as July slips, spreads edge highe.

text.p: Cash Brent was mixed in early Monday talk, with intermonth spreads firming slightly even as outright values slipped after Friday's rally, dealers said.
July Brent lost eight cents to $20.23 a barrel by 1007 GMT, after climbing over 80 cents in a late fund-led rally fuelled by strong technical indicators.
But intermonth spreads edged higher, June/July pegged at +2 cents after a deal at +1 late on Friday. July/August and Aug/Sep talked a couple of cents firmer at +4/+7 and +5/+8 respectively.
Brent contracts for difference (CFDs) were extremely quiet, but this week's dates were offered a couple of cents higher.
May 19-23 was talked at July -19/-16 cents from -20/-18 cents late on Friday.
Traders said Brent should continue to benefit from U.S. Gulf demand helped by a wide open arbitrage. The July Brent-WTI spread stood at a steady $1.70 a barrel early on Monday.
There was unconfirmed talk that a U.S. refiner/trader sold three Brent cargoes for third decade June arrival into the U.S. Gulf on Friday, in addition to a fourth sold earlier last week.
A Wall Street trader paid July Brent -29 cents on Friday for a May 28-30 Brent, but other end-month cargoes were offered firmer at around July -20 cents.
Three Brent cargoes, due to load June 3-5, were expected to pass through the paper chains on Monday, traders said.
Both Brents nominated loading dates on Friday were five o'clocked.
